# dotnet-inspect

A CLI tool for inspecting .NET assemblies and NuGet packages. Useful for understanding package contents, comparing API surfaces between versions, and auditing assemblies for SourceLink/determinism.

## Commands

### package - Inspect NuGet packages

```bash
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json                      # Package metadata
dotnet-inspect package System.CommandLine --files            # List DLLs
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --files --all        # List all files
dotnet-inspect package System.CommandLine --versions         # Available versions
dotnet-inspect package System.CommandLine --versions --preview -n 5  # With prereleases, limited
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json --deps               # Show dependencies
dotnet-inspect package dotnet-inspect --files --all          # Inspect tool packages
```

### assembly - Inspect .NET assemblies

```bash
dotnet-inspect assembly MyLib.dll                            # Basic info
dotnet-inspect assembly MyLib.dll --audit                    # SourceLink/determinism audit
dotnet-inspect assembly --package System.Text.Json --tfm net8.0  # From package by TFM
dotnet-inspect assembly --package System.CommandLine@2.0.2   # From specific version
dotnet-inspect assembly --package dotnet-inspect             # dotnet-inspect inspecting itself
```

### api - View public API surface

```bash
dotnet-inspect api --package System.CommandLine              # List all types (auto-selects highest TFM)
dotnet-inspect api --package System.Text.Json --tfm net8.0   # Specific TFM
dotnet-inspect api --package Spectre.Console --filter "Progress*"  # Filter types by glob pattern
dotnet-inspect api --package System.Text.Json --filter "*Serializer*"  # Find serializer-related types
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json # Specific type
dotnet-inspect api Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.2  # Specific version
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json -m Deserialize  # Filter to member
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json -m Serialize -m Deserialize  # Multiple members
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json -m Serialize --signatures-only  # Plain signatures
dotnet-inspect api JsonDocument --package System.Text.Json --interfaces  # Show interfaces
dotnet-inspect api Command --package System.CommandLine -m SetAction -v:q  # Quiet mode
dotnet-inspect api Command --package System.CommandLine --ctor  # Show constructors with enhanced details
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json --json --compact  # JSON output
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json --all  # Include hidden/obsolete members
dotnet-inspect api Unsafe --package System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe --unsafe  # Filter to unsafe methods
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package Newtonsoft.Json --docs  # Fetch documentation from source
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package Newtonsoft.Json --docs --browsable-urls  # Docs with /blob/ URLs for browsers
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package Newtonsoft.Json --fields-only  # Source URL only, no members
dotnet-inspect api CommandLineBuilder --package dotnet-inspect  # dotnet-inspect inspecting itself
```

### type - View type shape with hierarchy (tree view)

```bash
dotnet-inspect type JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json  # Type shape with inheritance, interfaces, members
dotnet-inspect type Command --package System.CommandLine       # Shows base class and implemented interfaces
dotnet-inspect type JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json --json  # JSON output
```

### diff - Compare API surfaces between versions

```bash
dotnet-inspect diff JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.0  # Compare type between versions
dotnet-inspect diff Command --package System.CommandLine@2.0.1..2.0.2        # See what changed
```

## Platform Assembly Inspection

Inspect .NET SDK reference assemblies directly without downloading packages:

```bash
# List installed frameworks and their versions
dotnet-inspect platform                                     # List installed frameworks
dotnet-inspect platform --list-versions                     # Show all installed versions
dotnet-inspect platform --framework runtime                 # List assemblies in runtime
dotnet-inspect platform --framework runtime@9.0.12          # Specific runtime version
dotnet-inspect platform --framework runtime --types         # Include public type counts

# Inspect platform assemblies with api command
dotnet-inspect api --platform System.Text.Json              # List types in platform assembly
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --platform System.Text.Json  # Specific type in platform assembly
dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --platform System.Text.Json --docs  # With XML documentation
dotnet-inspect api --platform System.Console --framework runtime@9.0.12  # Specific runtime version
dotnet-inspect api Span --platform System.Memory --framework runtime  # Types from any platform assembly
```

## Common Workflows

```bash
# Compare API between versions (built-in diff)
dotnet-inspect diff JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json@9.0.0..10.0.0

# Or use shell diff for line-by-line comparison
diff <(dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json@9.0.0) \
     <(dotnet-inspect api JsonSerializer --package System.Text.Json@10.0.0)
```

## Output Formats

- Default: Markdown tables with full method signatures including parameter names
- `--signatures-only`: Plain signatures only (no table formatting, minimal tokens)
- `--json`: JSON output
- `--json --compact`: Minified JSON, omits false/default values

## Output Control (Height × Width)

Output follows a 2D progressive disclosure model:
- **Width** (verbosity): `-v:q` → `-v:d` controls information density
- **Height** (sections): `-s:1,2` (include) or `-x:3` (exclude) controls which sections appear

### Verbosity Levels

| Level | Flag | Package Command Output |
|-------|------|------------------------|
| Quiet | `-v:q` or `-v quiet` | H1 title + compact line |
| Minimal | `-v:m` or `-v minimal` | H1 + description + compact line (default) |
| Normal | `-v:n` or `-v normal` | + Vulnerabilities section + Metadata table + tier 1 sections |
| Detailed | `-v:d` or `-v detailed` | + tier 2 sections (Files, Package Dependencies) |

### Compact Line Format

The compact line provides essential triage fields in a pipe-delimited format:

```
Type: Library | TFM: net8.0 | Updated: 2024-07-09 | Vulnerabilities: 1
```

Fields shown (when present):
- **Type**: Package type (Library, DotnetTool, etc.)
- **TFM**: Newest/highest target framework in the package
- **Updated**: Publication date from NuGet
- **Deprecated**: Deprecation reason (e.g., "Legacy - use NewPackage")
- **Vulnerabilities**: Count of known security vulnerabilities

All compact line fields are also included in the Metadata table at normal+ verbosity.

## Section Filtering

Filter by H2 section number (1-indexed). Use `-s:1,2` to include or `-x:3` to exclude.

```bash
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json -s:1       # Metadata only (exclude dependencies)
dotnet-inspect package System.Text.Json -v:d -s:1  # Detailed metadata only
```

## Tips

- Signatures include parameter names: `void Serialize(Stream utf8Json, TValue value, JsonSerializerOptions options)`
- Version suffix: `System.Text.Json@9.0.12`
- Assembly paths use forward slashes: `lib/net8.0/Foo.dll`
- `--tfm net8.0` selects by target framework; without it, highest TFM is auto-selected
- `-m`/`--member` filter is case-insensitive and shows all matching overloads
- `--filter` uses glob patterns: `*` matches any characters, `?` matches single character
- `--all` includes EditorBrowsable(Never) and Obsolete members (excluded by default)
- `--unsafe` filters to methods with pointer signatures (methods requiring unsafe context to call)
- `--ctor` shows constructors with enhanced output (parameter details, required vs optional)
- `--docs` fetches XML documentation comments from source via SourceLink
- `--browsable-urls` switches URLs from `/raw/` (302 redirect, LLM-friendly) to `/blob/` (browser-friendly)
- `--fields-only` shows only type info (source URL, docs) without member tables
- Source URLs use `/raw/` format by default, which returns raw file content via 302 redirect
- Platform assemblies (--platform) use .NET SDK reference assemblies; use --framework to specify runtime/aspnetcore/netstandard
- Tool packages have executables in `tools/net10.0/any/`; use `--files --all` to explore
- Reads from NuGet cache and caches downloads; use `--verbose` to see cache activity

## Generic Types

Generic types use CLR backtick notation internally. Both syntaxes are supported:

```bash
# C#-style syntax (automatically converted):
dotnet-inspect api 'Argument<T>' --package System.CommandLine
dotnet-inspect api 'Dictionary<TKey,TValue>' --package System.Collections

# CLR backtick notation (also works):
dotnet-inspect api 'Argument`1' --package System.CommandLine
dotnet-inspect api 'Dictionary`2' --package System.Collections
```

The backtick number indicates the arity (number of type parameters). Quotes are needed to escape special characters in most shells.

## Notes on Filtering

By default, the API output excludes:
- Members marked with `[EditorBrowsable(EditorBrowsableState.Never)]`
- Members marked with `[Obsolete]`

Use `--all` to include these members. Note that some libraries expose implementation-detail
methods as public without these attributes; these will still appear in the output.
